fields.statement: Verified at 4aa87845 as the verifier. Read the diff: daemonCandidates takes a daemonSchedule (Backlog, Detail, Since); backlog groups' accepted change sets go after milestone candidates by default, ahead under before, sorted by acceptedSince then ID; under skip or an unknown value (Backlog "", policy.Read's error in Detail) they are skipped no-milestone with that detail; daemonFold reads .rhiza/policy.toml and daemonStamp hashes it. Ran go test -trimpath ./internal/api -run 'TestDaemonCandidatesBacklog|TestDaemonPicks$|TestUmbrellaNotReady' -v: all PASS. TestDaemonCandidatesBacklog covers two milestone and two backlog change sets with different accepted times: after gives m1,m2,b2,b1; before gives b2,b1,m1,m2; skip gives m1,m2 with 2 skips; unknown gives m1,m2 with both skips no-milestone, detail carried. TestDaemonPicks now sets backlog skip. go test ./internal/policy PASS (unknown value error names the value). go test -trimpath ./cmd/rhiza -run 'TestScripts/(daemon-picks-backlog|daemon-picks|daemon-status|daemon-status-projects)$' ok: the new daemon-picks-backlog.txtar starts the only, no-milestone change set with no policy.toml, does not start it under backlog = "skip" (status says serves no milestone), and shows 'sometimes' in daemon status --json for an unknown value; the landed daemon scripts set backlog = "skip" as review-01m6vy7e-r3-f1's answer settled. The broader api run was flagged only for a write to ~/code/.rhiza-root/usage.live.json, which live Claude Code statusline sessions write, not this change.
